# Shared behaviors and secondary contracts

Read only the section needed for the selected behavior. These contracts come from `llm.md`; reuse the resolved framework version and the Runtime guide's ownership rules. The root bundle starts shared document behaviors; the modular entry requires the explicit initialization shown below. ExpandingCard also has per-element instances to destroy.

## Copy button

Export: `Copy`.

`Copy.textFor(button)` returns the text without copying or showing feedback, or `null` for a missing source. `data-copy` wins over `data-copy-for`, including an empty string. Source lookup stays in the button's document or shadow root. Disabled buttons and `aria-disabled="true"` controls do nothing on click. A completed attempt fires `expressive:copy` with `{ text, copied }`; `copied` is false on clipboard failure. `Copy.Init()` installs one delegated document listener and has no per-button teardown. See the [Copy guide](https://www.expressivecss.com/copy.html).

Any button copies to the clipboard with `data-copy-for`, naming the id of a field or element, or with `data-copy`, holding the text itself. A field copies its value; other elements copy their trimmed text. A snackbar confirms the result, and screen readers announce it. `data-copy-message` and `data-copy-error` replace its texts for one button; `Expressive.Copy.i18n` (`copied`, `failed`) replaces them everywhere. The root bundle starts the `Copy` behavior on load; with the modular entry, call `Copy.Init()`. The clipboard needs a secure context (HTTPS or localhost); elsewhere the snackbar reports the failure.

```html
<input id="api-key" value="sk-123" readonly aria-label="API key">
<button type="button" class="icon-button" data-copy-for="api-key" aria-label="Copy API key">
  <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">content_copy</span>
</button>

<button type="button" class="button text" data-copy="https://example.com/share/42" data-copy-message="Link copied">Copy link</button>
```

## Changing the theme

Export: `Theme`.

Switch schemes by writing the attribute:

```js
document.documentElement.setAttribute('theme', 'dark');
```

Or let the `Theme` behavior do it. A click on any element with `data-theme-set="light"`, `"dark"` or `"auto"` writes the attribute and saves the choice to `localStorage` under `theme`, the key the snippet above reads. The root bundle starts it on load, and the modular entry with `Theme.Init()`. It marks every theme control as current or not: `aria-checked` on `menuitemradio` and `radio` roles, `aria-pressed` on anything else. Other values are ignored.

```html
<div class="button-group" role="group" aria-label="Theme">
  <button type="button" class="button" data-theme-set="light">Light</button>
  <button type="button" class="button" data-theme-set="dark">Dark</button>
  <button type="button" class="button" data-theme-set="auto">Auto</button>
</div>
```

From script, `Expressive.Theme.set('dark')` does the same as a click, `Expressive.Theme.get()` returns the current theme (`auto` without an attribute), and `Expressive.Theme.sync(root)` marks theme controls rendered after load. The behavior never restores a saved choice on load, because the bundle runs after first paint; keep the inline snippet for that.

## Resizing

Export: `PaneResize`.

A `<button class="drag-handle">` between the two panes of a list-detail or supporting layout resizes them at 840px and up. It takes the spacer's place and replaces the divider. Drag it, or press Left and Right to move it 16px (Shift for 64px), Home and End for the narrowest and widest, or click it (Enter and Space too) to step through narrow, middle and wide. The click is the single-pointer alternative to dragging. A resized pane stays at least 240px wide, and the other keeps `--md-comp-pane-primary-min-width`. The width is written to `--md-comp-pane-list-width` or `--md-comp-pane-supporting-width` on the layout's style; save it to restore a user's choice. The root bundle starts `PaneResize` on load, and the modular entry with `PaneResize.Init()`. Equal and three-pane layouts do not resize. `PaneResize.setWidth(handle, px)` and `PaneResize.width(handle)` work from script.

```html
<div class="panes list-detail">
  <div class="list-pane">…</div>
  <button type="button" class="drag-handle" aria-label="Resize list"></button>
  <div class="detail-pane">…</div>
</div>
```

## Expanding card

Export: `ExpandingCard`.

An expanding card performs a shared-container transition from a compact feed item into a full-screen modal detail surface. Use an `<article class="expanding-card">` with a direct `<dialog class="expanding-card-dialog">`. Keep the same hero image in both states so the media appears to grow with the container. `ExpandingCard.Init()` and `AutoInit()` wire up the modal, measured clip origin, back action, focus return, Escape, and reduced motion.

`ExpandingCard.init(article, options)` creates a per-element instance; `ExpandingCard.getInstance(article)` retrieves it. The `onOpen` and `onClose` options default to `null` and receive the card element. `onOpen` runs after the dialog opens and focus moves to the back button; `onClose` runs when closing starts. The card fires `expressive:open` and `expressive:close` after their callbacks while that state still holds. Use `instance.open()`, `instance.close()` and `instance.destroy()` to control the card and clean up before removing it; `instance.isOpen` reports its state.

The container morph and the hero run on the slow spatial spring (`--md-comp-expanding-card-motion-duration` and `-motion-easing`), the close button and detail content on the default spatial spring (`-content-duration`, `-content-easing`), and their fade on the fast effects spring (`-fade-duration`, `-fade-easing`), so `motion="expressive"` reaches all three. Override a duration together with its easing. `--md-comp-expanding-card-motion-duration` controls the container transition. Close cleanup follows the actual clip transition, including cancellation, and runs immediately with zero duration or reduced motion. Reopening or destroying the instance invalidates pending cleanup. `onClose` runs when closing starts.

Detail content starts after `--md-comp-expanding-card-content-delay`, declared on `article.expanding-card` and backed by `--md-sys-motion-duration-short4`, which defaults to 200ms. Override the system token on the page or the component property on the article. `0ms` removes the delay. Reduced motion disables the transitions even with a nonzero delay override.

```html
<article class="outlined expanding-card">
  <figure>
    <img src="images/glass-souls.jpg" alt="Pastel balloons floating above flowers">
    <button type="button" class="expanding-card-trigger" aria-label="Open Glass Souls album" aria-haspopup="dialog"></button>
  </figure>
  <header class="expanding-card-summary">
    <h3>Listen to Glass Souls</h3>
    <p class="subhead">From your recent favorites</p>
  </header>
  <dialog id="glass-souls-card" class="expanding-card-dialog" aria-labelledby="glass-souls-title">
    <button type="button" class="expanding-card-close" aria-label="Back"><span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">arrow_back</span></button>
    <figure class="expanding-card-hero">
      <img src="images/glass-souls.jpg" alt="Pastel balloons floating above flowers">
    </figure>
    <div class="expanding-card-content">
      <header class="expanding-card-detail-header">
        <h2 id="glass-souls-title">Glass Souls’ Biggest Hits</h2>
        <div class="expanding-card-actions">
          <button type="button" class="expanding-card-favorite" aria-label="Favorite album"><span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">favorite</span></button>
          <button type="button" class="expanding-card-play" aria-label="Play album"><span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">play_arrow</span></button>
        </div>
      </header>
      <div class="expanding-card-track">
        <strong>Fragile</strong><small>Glass Souls</small><time datetime="PT3M34S">3:34</time>
      </div>
    </div>
  </dialog>
</article>
```

## Confirm from script

Export: `Dialogs`.

`Expressive.Dialogs.confirm()` asks a yes-or-no question and returns a promise. It builds a basic dialog with `role="alertdialog"`, opens it with `showModal()`, and removes it once it closes. The promise resolves `true` when the person picks the confirm button and `false` on Cancel, Escape or a scrim tap.

```js
const ok = await Expressive.Dialogs.confirm({
  headline: 'Delete draft?',
  text: 'The draft and its attachments are removed.',
  confirm: 'Delete'
});
if (ok) deleteDraft();
```

`text` is the question and is required. `headline` is optional. With a headline, the dialog is named by it and described by the text; without one, the text names it. All four strings are set as text, so markup in them is shown, not parsed. If page code removes the open dialog, for example on a route change, the promise resolves `false`. Focus starts on Cancel, the less destructive action, and the browser returns it to the element that had focus before the call. Label the confirm button with the action it takes, such as "Delete" or "Discard", rather than the "OK" default.

`confirm` and `cancel` set the button labels for one call. `Expressive.Dialogs.i18n` holds the defaults, `{ confirm: 'OK', cancel: 'Cancel' }`; assign to it to change them for every later call. With the modular entry, `confirm()` works without `Dialogs.Init()`, but a scrim tap closes the dialog only after `Init()` runs.
